thread:
maria: Heads up — started seeing east-west p95 spikes ~08:12 UTC in cluster-phi during the peak batching window. p95 jumped to ~140ms between gpu-pool nodes, causing a few inference timeouts. Anyone else seeing this?
aj: seeing the same on phi-03 -> phi-07 path. Pods on gpu-pool reported grpc deadline exceeded then recovered. :eye_speech_bubble:
sanjay: looked at node metrics — tx_errors and rx_errors are low, but netdev drops increased on phi-07 around the same time. attaching quick counters: `ifconfig ens5: tx 12 rx 9 drop 84`
taylor: deploying logs — not a model change. Deploy-bot shows a config rollout 07:58 UTC for CNI tweaks (we moved to ovn 2.13 last night). ops-bot: deploy/infra-cni v2.13 -> success @ 07:58:11 UTC.
maria: hmm CNI change + first big peak after morning traffic ramp. Could be OVS datapath path length or offload interaction. Can someone run ethtool and dmesg on phi-07?
kevin: running: `ssh phi-07 sudo ethtool -S ens5 | egrep "rx_|tx_|drop"` -> gives a burst of rx_dropped: 78 at 08:12:14. Also `dmesg | tail -n 50` shows a couple of mlx5_core: event QP error messages around that time.
sanjay: QP errors smell like RDMA queue pair flaps. Are we using IPoIB or RoCE? phi pool is RoCEv2 on Mellanox. Could be ECN or MTU mismatch on a subset of leafs.
irene: I saw a concurrent spike in GSO/GRO counters on the top-of-rack — maybe LRO/GRO coalescing producing large packets that the RDMA stack doesn't like. Ianned a pcap: large segmented packets then retransmits.
aj: quick test — temporarily disabled GRO on phi-07 and phi-03 for 10s: `sudo ethtool -K ens5 gro off` then re-ran a 1min load. p95 dropped back to ~28ms. Re-enabled after. That points to offload interactions.
maria: good repro. Does disabling GRO degrade throughput under normal loads? We need a mitigation that doesn't regress steady-state.
taylor: can we roll a kernel module parameter to force work around? There was a kernel bump last week on the nodes (5.19.16 -> 5.19.18). Maybe regression.
kevin: created quick iperf between phi-03 and phi-07 with and without GRO: with GRO p95=125ms, without p95=22ms. Logs here: `iperf -c phi-07 -t 60 -P 8`.
sanjay: two action candidates: 1) temporarily disable GRO/GSO on affected fleet during peak window via daemonset, 2) pin flows to a trunk path that avoids T1 switch where RX drops observed, 3) open ticket with NIC vendor about RDMA QP errors + kernel bump.
irene: +1 for 1) as immediate mitigation. We should also run targeted MTU checks across all leafs: `ip link show | grep mtu` and confirm no 9000 vs 9216 mismatch.
aj: I can push a canary daemonset to 10% of gpu-pool nodes to toggle `ethtool -K ens5 gro off gso off` around the 08:00-09:30 window tomorrow. Want to watch for side effects.
maria: please do canary. Also add per-pod timeouts to be more graceful until we fix. Open a scheduled runbook for on-call with commands and rollback.
kevin: filed infra ticket INF-4271 with uplink vendor and attached dmesg + pcap, flagged as P1 for impact during batching windows.
ops-bot: incident created INF-4271 (P1) by kevin at 1923459875. Assigned: network-eng.
taylor: FYI we have some nodes with slightly different MTU (9212 vs 9216) detected last week during inventory scan — could be leftover from old provisioning image. I'll add that to the check list.
sanjay: timeline so far: 07:58 CNI rollout, 08:12 latency spike, 08:20 GRO toggle repro, 08:35 canary suggested. Next: canary tomorrow, vendor ticket, fleet MTU audit.
maria: thanks all. If canary looks good, we'll schedule a rolling fleet mitigation and follow up with vendor for kernel/firmware fix. :thumbsup:
